summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) building real-time Edge AI systems for robotics, optimizing inference latency with CUDA and TensorRT. Experienced deploying perception and ASR pipelines on Jetson-class devices under compute and network constraints, and closing the loop into embedded control on STM32/Arduino. Comfortable across the stack: C/C++, ROS2, and register-level embedded firmware.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control, interfacing ADXL345 accelerometers with a Raspberry Pi over I2C and streaming motion data via HC-05 Bluetooth to HID commands.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration.

experience.title: Deep Learning Intern
bullets: Curated and annotated a custom object detection dataset; trained YOLOv8n on 1,133 images achieving 83% mAP@50 on held-out validation.
Exported the trained model to ONNX and TFLite for real-time mobile/edge deployment.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end to end.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided pick-and-place robot over a three-layer distributed pipeline: Flutter client, Flask-SocketIO edge server, and Jetson+Arduino controller over a unified WebSocket fabric.

Integrated faster-whisper STT (1.0-1.4s), Gemini intent classification (<500ms), and TensorRT-optimized YOLO for visual servoing, achieving a 5.2x speedup (56.7→10.9 ms, 17.6→92 FPS) over eager PyTorch.
Added dual VL53L0X ToF sensors for contact-aware grasping via I2C mux; resolved 11 integration failures to reach 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++, driving five servos with range-gated contact detection.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to an STM32 over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands; used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination and integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing.

projects.name: ROS-Based Robotic Arm (AL5B & UR5e)
bullets: Derived DH tables and hand-computed full forward kinematic chains for a 6-DoF UR5e and 5-DoF AL5B; validated against MoveIt and RViz URDF models in ROS 2 Humble and ROS Noetic.
Planned and executed collision-free pick-and-place trajectories on a physical UR5e; measured AL5B repeatability at <2mm over 10 trials.
